meta.move: Strong path: owns the missed call, then evidence in order, then the rewrite
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have about twenty minutes, and I'd like to know who decided on the zero, and whether anyone spoke to Owen before it went in.
Ms. Kalinowski, thank you for coming in. Before anything else: I entered that zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. Then it's coming off, and I want that in writing. What did you base it on?

Here's what I can show you. The document's version history: created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, title only. At 11:52, 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58, another 794. No drafts before that.
Writing sample or not, 4.2 says someone calls me before a mark goes in, and nobody did. So who decided, and was Owen heard first?
Second, the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the scene; you can search it yourself.
I'm searching it now, and I'm writing down that you showed me the scene. Students misquote plays all the time, Hale, so what exactly does one bad line prove?

Our procedure allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. We could do it in my room, Thursday at 8:15, with the vice-principal supervising.

Fine. Thursday at 8:15, in your room, with the vice-principal, no other students, and I'll take it to put this behind him. I want it in an email tonight that the zero comes off the gradebook now and nothing goes on his record, copied to the principal.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You apologised for entering the zero before calling me, and you offered a supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15 in your room with the vice-principal, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing going on Owen's record. I still require written confirmation tonight that the zero is off the gradebook now, that no other students will be present, and that nothing is placed in his file. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15 with the vice-principal, and she still wants it in writing that the zero comes off now and nothing goes on his record. That is the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record, which is procedure 4.4.
What moved her: You showed her a misquoted line from the play that she could search herself, which gave her something dated and checkable instead of a score.
What cost ground: Nothing clearly did, since you owned the zero in one sentence at the start and never accused Owen of anything.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your evidence about edits late the night before the due date came close to that night, and she answered by going straight to procedure. It proves nothing about the essay, and it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked what one bad line proves, you moved to the rewrite without answering her, so answer that question first before offering the way out.
